exercise.instruction: Write the program: define struct Contact with public std::string name and std::string phone. In main create std::vector<Contact> contacts and push_back Bob first ({"Bob", "555-0102"}) then Alice ({"Alice", "555-0101"}). Sort by name with std::sort and a lambda comparing a.name < b.name, then print each contact's name on its own line.
hints: Hint 1: struct Contact { std::string name; std::string phone; };
Hint 3: std::sort(contacts.begin(), contacts.end(), [](const Contact& a, const Contact& b) { return a.name < b.name; });
Hint 4: for (const Contact& c : contacts) { std::cout << c.name << std::endl; }

quiz.question: Why store a contact as a struct?
options: It keeps name and phone together as one unit

quiz.question: Why pass a lambda to std::sort here?
